bibl.title: Towards a Translocal Elite Culture in the Ptolemaic Empire.
bibl.seg: Christelle Fischer-Bovet, Towards a Translocal Elite Culture in the Ptolemaic Empire.

Myles Lavan, Richard E. Payne & John Weisweiler (edd.), Cosmopolitanism and Empire: Universal Rulers, Local Elites, and Cultural Integration in the Ancient Near East and Mediterranean = Oxford Studies in Early Empires (Oxford, 2016) pp. 103-128, fig.
bibl.note: Introduction. - The localist mode of expression: Greek and hellenized cities; - Egyptian priests. - Translocal culture and ideology: The trilingual decrees; - The royal and dynastic cults; - Royal festivals and the creation of translocal space and time; - The birthday of the king as the beginning of good things for all mankind; - The return of the statues carried away by the Persians; - Trilingual decrees, translocal constructions; - Translocal individuals? - Conclusion.
